Four leads are recalled for checking: the vendor's own validation report, a descriptive study of command centre escalation, an overview of emergency prediction models and a study of night-time performance. items.title: Vendor validation report for an admission boarding risk score
items.keyFindings: Reports high discrimination for predicting boarding over four hours in the vendor's development hospitals.
items.limitations: Recalled lead; written by the vendor; no external sites.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; probably one of the two hits the provider did not return.

items.title: Command centre dashboards and bed management escalation: a descriptive study
items.keyFindings: Describes how bed managers respond to flagged patients on a command centre display; escalation was more frequent for flagged surgical patients.
items.limitations: Recalled lead with no year, grade or method quality; descriptive only.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; year not known.

items.title: Prediction models for hospital admission and bed wait from the emergency department: a scoping overview
items.authors: Lindqvist-Osei M, Carvalho-Mbeki J, Petit-Rourke A
items.keyFindings: Most published models predicted admission rather than bed wait, and few were externally validated.

items.title: Night-time boarding and staffing: why models trained on daytime data fail after midnight
items.keyFindings: Reports poorer discrimination for night admissions because discharges and bed cleaning stop overnight.

summary: Four unchecked leads; no certainty proposed.
